title: VPC security patterns and SIEM integration playbook
content:
Operational hardening playbook: VPC security patterns + RBAC v2 mapping + audit schema + SIEM export + evidence automation

Purpose:
This playbook is intended for the Private deployment team and SREs running customer air-gapped or VPC-hosted Redwood clusters. It consolidates recommended VPC patterns, firewall rule templates, mutual TLS considerations, RBAC v2 role-to-service mappings, a normalized audit log schema, SIEM export mappings, and an evidence automation checklist for compliance reviews. Use as a working reference; many sections are intentionally terse to be copy/pasted into templates and runbooks.

Scope:
- Intra-VPC segmentation for inference clusters, control plane, and observability stacks.
- Network policy and firewall rules for least privilege egress/ingress.
- mTLS bootstrap and rotation guidance for service-to-service auth.
- RBAC v2 mapping: operators, admins, support, telemetry ingestion.
- Audit log schema (flattened JSON) and recommended retention fields.
- SIEM export: field mappings and example Splunk/Elastic ingestion spec.
- Evidence automation: playbook to collect, validate, and archive proof artifacts for audits.

1) High-level VPC pattern (3-tier zero-trust):
- Management VPC (control plane): API, management UI, bootstrap services. Private endpoints; pair with management bastion.
- Compute VPC (served models): GPU pools, inference nodes, KV cache. Strict egress; only to approved artifact registries and telemetry endpoints.
- Observability VPC (metrics/logs/siem): telemetry collectors, SIEM forwarders, storage. Peered with Management VPC via strict routes.

Peering model: use transit gateway or VPC peering with explicit route tables. Avoid broad 0.0.0.0/0 peering. All peering must go through firewall/NAT VMs for inspection for regulated customers.

ASCII diagram (simplified):

[Management VPC] --(mgmt-bastion)--> [Transit GW / Firewall HA] <--(peer)-- [Compute VPC] <--(egress to artifacts)--> [Artifact Mirror / Registry]
                             
                             `--(forward)--> [Observability VPC: SIEM-forwarder, metrics-infra]

2) Firewall rule templates (principle: explicit allow, deny by default)
- Management VPC (control-plane-api):
  - inbound: allow 443 from customer-admin-bastion-cidrs; allow 22 only from jump-hosts (temporary rule TTL)
  - outbound: allow 443 to artifact-registry-cidrs; allow 443 to SIEM-forwarder IPs; deny all else
- Compute VPC (inference nodes):
  - inbound: allow 1024-65535 from model-gateway subnets for RPCs; allow 443 only from load-balancer IPs
  - outbound: allow 443 to artifact-mirrors; allow 53 to internal DNS; allow 123 to NTP endpoints; block internet egress except to whitelisted endpoints
- Observability VPC:
  - inbound: allow 6514 (TLS syslog) from collector IPs; allow 9200/9300 internal ES traffic only from trusted subnets
  - outbound: allow 443 to SIEM SaaS collectors; allow 9000 to blob storage for archive

Rule metadata: each firewall rule must have: owner, justification, Jira ticket id, TTL (optional), evidence_link after change. Enforce via IaC (terraform) with PR reviews.

3) mTLS patterns and bootstrap:
- Purpose: mutual auth for inter-service RPCs (model-gateway <-> inference-node, inference-node <-> kv-cache, telemetry-collector <-> forwarder) to prevent token theft and unauthorized egress.
- Certs: short-lived leaf certs (1-7 days) issued by private CA; CA keys in HSM/KMS.
- Bootstrapping: node generates CSR, authenticated to CA via instance identity (e.g., cloud instance metadata + signed attestation), CA returns cert and cert-chain.
- Rotation: staggered rolling rotation with overlap window; cert revocation via CRL + OCSP responder inside Management VPC.
- Transport: TLS1.3 required, only AEAD ciphers allowed; disable TLS resumption for sensitive channels where identity must be re-checked.
- Implementation notes: use SPIFFE/SPIRE for workload identity where possible; fallback to Vault PKI for smaller installs.

mTLS checklist (quick):
- [ ] CA root in KMS/HSM + offline backup stored in secure vault
- [ ] Automated CSR flow tested in staging
- [ ] OCSP responder reachable only from Management and Observability VPCs
- [ ] CRL rotation schedule established
- [ ] Certificates issued with correct SANs (service names + cluster id)

4) RBAC v2 mapping (roles -> permissions -> typical assignment):
- role: infra-operator (cluster-level) -> perms: start/stop nodes, change autoscale, update terraform apply. Assigned to: infra-oncall group.
- role: controlplane-admin -> perms: update model manifest, create rollouts, access control-plane API. Assigned to: platform-eng leads.
- role: support-readonly -> perms: read logs, read metrics, read config. Assigned to: customer-success L1/L2.
- role: telemetry-ingest -> perms: write telemetry, rotate ingestion keys. Assigned to: observability services.
- role: compliance-auditor -> perms: read audit-logs, export evidence bundles. Assigned to: security/compliance team, ephemeral access via short-lived tokens.

Notes: RBAC v2 must implement resource scoping: project/customer -> cluster -> model. Avoid cluster-wide wildcard permissions where possible. Map service accounts to RBAC roles and use least privilege for service principals.

5) Audit log schema (normalized flattened JSON for SIEM ingestion)
- Fields to emit for every significant event:
  - timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
  - event_id (uuidv4)
  - actor_id (user|service id)
  - actor_type (human|service|operator)
  - action (string, e.g., "model.deploy", "node.terminate", "cert.request")
  - resource_type (cluster|node|model|secret|firewall-rule)
  - resource_id (ARN-style or cluster:namespace:name)
  - before_state (url to snapshot OR base64-diff)
  - after_state (url to snapshot OR base64-diff)
  - outcome (success|failure|partial)
  - ip (source ip)
  - user_agent (if applicable)
  - request_id (trace-id)
  - location (region, az)
  - ticket (linked jira id, optional)
  - reason (free text justification captured at change time)

Example single-line event (flattened):
{"timestamp":"2026-02-14T21:04:02Z","event_id":"b7c1f9f2-1a2b-4c6e-9d3f-0a1b2c3d4e5f","actor_id":"svc-telemetry-12","actor_type":"service","action":"telemetry.forwarder.config.update","resource_type":"config","resource_id":"cluster:prod-nyc:telemetry-config","outcome":"success","ip":"10.0.34.12","request_id":"trace-9f8e7d6c","location":"us-east1","ticket":"JIRA-PRIVATEDEP-7123","reason":"enable splunk forwarder for customer X"}

6) SIEM export mapping (example for Elastic ingestion):
- index: redwood-audit-YYYY.MM.DD
- pipeline: audit-normalize-pipeline (use ingest node to parse timestamp and set types)
- field mappings: timestamp -> @timestamp, event_id -> event.id, actor_id -> user.id, actor_type -> user.type, action -> event.action, resource_type -> kubernetes.resource.type (or custom), resource_id -> resource.id, outcome -> event.outcome, ip -> source.ip, request_id -> trace.id, ticket -> labels.jira

Example Filebeat/Fluentd hint: label events with cluster and customer id early to avoid expensive enrichments later. Forwarder config should compress and sign batches with mTLS to SIEM-forwarder.

7) Evidence automation runbook (collect, validate, sign, store)
- Objective: produce an immutable evidence bundle for audit windows (e.g., quarterly) that proves: firewall rules as-of date, cert rotation logs, RBAC grants at snapshot time, audit log slices, SIEM export receipts, terraform plan/apply history.
- Steps:
  1. Trigger snapshot job (cron) in Management VPC.
  2. Collect artifacts: terraform state, firewall rule configs (read-only), CA issuance logs, OCSP/CRL snapshots, RBAC grant dump (RBAC v2 export), audit-log slice (time window).
  3. Validate artifacts: run schema checks (audit schema above), run RBAC least-privilege linter, ensure CA chain validated, verify SIEM receipts for all forwarded events.
  4. Sign bundle: produce tar.gz, sign with archive key from KMS (detached signature), store signature plus checksum metadata file.
  5. Push to WORM storage (immutable blob) in Observability VPC and to customer-provided archive if required.
  6. Emit change ticket: attach evidence bundle id to Jira ticket per compliance requirement.

Automation hints: implement as serverless job in Management VPC with ephemeral role escalation to read-only buckets. Use attestations (signed by instance metadata + CI/CD pipeline) for provenance.

8) Operational playbook snippets (for oncall):
- If unexpected egress detected from compute VPC to unknown IP: immediately apply egress block rule, snapshot connection logs, collect audit-events for last 24h, notify security channel.
- If cert expiry approaching with failed rotate: escalate to infra-operator, enable manual cert issuance script, create temporary allowlist for necessary bootstrap.
- When SIEM ingestion drops: check forwarder certificate validity, network ACLs between compute & observability VPCs, check queue backlog on forwarder.

9) Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we adopt SPIFFE by default for all private deployments? (Mei: evaluate carriers for on-prem installs)
- Automate RBAC snapshot diffs and surface high-privilege changes to Slack channel? (Liam: prototype)
- Define standardized TTLs for firewall temporary rules (default 48h) and automated reclamation.

Appendix: quick links (internal)
- Compliance checklist template: CONFLUENCE-PRIVATE-VPC-CHECKS
- Terraform firewall module: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/modules/firewall-v2
- SIEM parser repo: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/siem-parsers

Notes to reviewer: this is intentionally pragmatic and contains runnable snippets/fields meant to be copied into IaC and log pipelines. Please flag any missing fields for Elastic/Splunk ingestion or additional RBAC role edge cases.

-- Samira
